    The weighted average fair value of options granted was $6.70 for
    the year ended December&#160;31, 2006, $2.59 for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2005 and $4.20 for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2004. The intrinsic value of options exercised
    was approximately $7.9&#160;million during the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2006, $4.2&#160;million during the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2005 and $0.1&#160;million during the year
    ended December&#160;31, 2004. Intrinsic value is the difference
    between the Company&#146;s closing stock price on the day the
    options were exercised and the exercise price, multiplied by the
    number of options exercised. Proceeds received from option
    exercises for the year ended December&#160;31, 2006 were
    $4.1&#160;million.

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    At December&#160;31, 2006, unrecognized compensation expense
    relating to non-vested options totaled $14.9&#160;million. This
    expense is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average
    period of three years.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company&#146;s Employee Stock Purchase Plan, or ESPP,
    provides for 1,000,000&#160;shares of the Company&#146;s
    Class&#160;A common stock to be reserved for issuance upon
    exercise of purchase rights which may be granted under the ESPP.
    The ESPP is designed to encourage stock ownership by the
    Company&#146;s employees. Employees elect to participate in the
    plan semi-annually. The plan period is six months. Shares are
    purchased at 85% of the market price of the Company&#146;s
    Class&#160;A common stock. The price is determined as the lower
    of the price at the initial date or at the end of the six-month
    period. The fair value of shares offered through the ESPP is
    estimated and recognized over each semi-annual participation
    period.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company adopted the modified prospective transition method
    provided for under SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123(R), and consequently
    has not retroactively adjusted results of prior periods. This
    adoption resulted in the recognition of share-based compensation
    totaling approximately $7.6&#160;million ($4.7&#160;million, net
    of income tax) for the year ended December&#160;31, 2006. Prior
    to 2006 under APB Opinion No.&#160;25, the pro forma expense for
    the Company&#146;s stock options and ESPP had been calculated
    consistent with SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123(R). Therefore, had
    compensation expense

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On February&#160;17, 2004, the Company transferred its ownership
    in Maryland 2 RSA wireless property in exchange for Cingular
    Wireless&#146; ownership in Michigan 5 RSA wireless property,
    $22.0&#160;million in cash and Cingular Wireless&#146;
    one-percent ownership interest in Texas 2 RSA and Oklahoma 5 and
    7 RSAs. The Company is the majority owner of these three
    partnerships. The Company accounted for the exchange as a sale
    of Maryland 2 RSA and a purchase of Michigan 5 RSA. Therefore,
    the Michigan 5 RSA assets, liabilities and results of operations
    have only been included in the accompanying consolidated
    financials from the date of acquisition, February&#160;17, 2004.
    The Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements were
    reclassified for all periods presented to reflect the
    operations, assets and liabilities of the Maryland 2 RSA
    wireless property as discontinued operations.
</DIV>

    in Maryland 2 RSA wireless property in exchange for Cingular

    in Note&#160;4.

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On June&#160;15, 2004, the Company acquired certain assets,
    principally PCS licenses and an existing GSM network, of
    NPI-Omnipoint Wireless, LLC, or NPI, for approximately
    $29.5&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    of the Michigan wireless assets of RFB and certain affiliates
    for $29.3&#160;million. RFB is made up of Michigan 2 RSA and
    Michigan 4 RSA. The Company purchased these assets in an auction
    conducted under Sections&#160;363 and 365 of the
    U.S.&#160;bankruptcy code. Upon

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    closing, the Company obtained control over most of these assets;
    however, assignment of certain spectrum licenses required FCC
    approval, for which the Company applied. The Company leased the
    RFB spectrum under a long-term spectrum management lease until
    it was awarded these licenses on June&#160;14, 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On September&#160;13, 2005, ACC acquired the non-license
    wireless assets of Endless Mountains Wireless, LLC in
    Pennsylvania 4 RSA. The Company operated Endless Mountains&#146;
    licensed 850&#160;MHz spectrum under a spectrum manager lease
    until it was granted FCC approval and acquired the spectrum on
    June&#160;13, 2006. The total purchase price for all acquired
    assets, including the FCC license, was approximately
    $12.2&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On May&#160;30, 2006, ACC purchased the non-spectrum assets of
    Texas 15 RSA. In addition, on June&#160;29, 2006, ACC closed on
    cellular and PCS spectrum covering the Texas 15 RSA and on
    additional PCS spectrum in the Texas counties of Brown,
    Comanche, Mills and Tom Green after receiving FCC approval. The
    total purchase price for these assets was approximately
    $25.4&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On August&#160;2, 2006, DCS completed the purchase of the
    wireless assets in Kodiak, Alaska of New Horizons Telecom, Inc.
    and Kodiak Electric Association, Inc. and the wireless assets in
    Nome, Alaska of Sitnasuak Native Corporation and SNC
    Telecommunications, Inc. The total purchase price for these
    assets was approximately $2.1&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;5, 2006, ACC acquired Highland Cellular LLC,
    which provides wireless service to West Virginia 7 RSA, and four
    adjacent counties in West Virginia 6 RSA and Virginia 2 RSA. In
    addition, Highland Cellular owns PCS spectrum in Virginia and
    West Virginia. The currently served markets and additional
    spectrum are primarily south of markets that the Company owns
    and operates in western Maryland, southern Ohio, southern
    Pennsylvania and West Virginia. As a result of the merger,
    Highland Cellular became a wholly owned subsidiary of ACC. The
    total purchase price for Highland Cellular was approximately
    $95.0&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;19, 2006, ACC made the final payment on 85
    Advanced Wireless Services, or AWS, licenses for which ACC was
    the winning bidder in the FCC&#146;s Auction 66. The auction was
    conducted during the summer and fall of 2006. These licenses,
    which are located in portions of Alaska, Kansas, Kentucky,
    Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Mexico, New York,
    Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia and
    Wisconsin, add incremental service areas to the Company&#146;s
    current coverage, as well as additional spectrum in areas that
    the Company currently serves in order to have capacity for
    increased voice and data transmission. The cost to ACC for these
    licenses was approximately $65.9&#160;million. Licensing from
    the FCC occurred on November&#160;29, 2006. Cash used for these
    transactions came from cash flows from operations, cash on hand
    and cash advanced from the credit facility obtained by ACC.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The above business combinations were accounted for as purchases.
    Accordingly, the related statements of financial position and
    results of operations have been included in the accompanying
    consolidated statements of operations from the date of
    acquisition. The unaudited pro forma financial information
    related to the Company&#146;s acquisitions has not been
    presented because these acquisitions, individually or in
    aggregate were not significant to the Company&#146;s
    consolidated results of operations.
</DIV>

    On September&#160;13, 2005, the Company completed its offerings
    of $150.0&#160;million principal amount of senior floating rate
    notes due 2012 and $150.0&#160;million principal amount of
    senior convertible debentures due 2025. The net proceeds from
    the offerings, before expenses, were $294.0&#160;million. In
    addition, the Company had granted the initial purchasers of the
    senior convertible debentures an option to purchase up to an
    additional $30.0&#160;million principal amount of senior
    convertible debentures. On October&#160;13, 2005, the initial
    purchasers exercised their right to purchase an additional
    $10.0&#160;million principal amount of debentures. Therefore, at
    December&#160;31, 2006, the aggregate principal amount of senior
    convertible debentures outstanding was $160.0&#160;million.

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    Senior Floating Rate Notes</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The senior floating rate notes, which mature on October&#160;15,
    2012, bear interest at the rate per annum equal to LIBOR plus
    4.25%, which is reset quarterly. Interest payments are due on
    January&#160;15, April&#160;15, July 15 and October&#160;15,
    commencing October&#160;15, 2005. The notes are effectively
    subordinated to DCC&#146;s existing and future secured
    indebtedness to the extent of the collateral securing that
    indebtedness, and to the existing and future liabilities of
    DCC&#146;s subsidiaries; equal in right of payment to all of
    DCC&#146;s existing and future unsecured senior indebtedness;
    and senior in right of payment to DCC&#146;s future subordinated
    indebtedness. At December&#160;31, 2006, LIBOR equaled 5.37%;
    therefore, the interest rate on these notes was 9.62%.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">DCC
    1.50%&#160;Senior Convertible Debentures</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The senior convertible debentures, which mature on
    October&#160;1, 2025, bear interest at 1.50%&#160;per annum.
    Prior to maturity, the holders can require redemption of the
    notes. This can occur on the anniversary date in 2010, 2015, or
    2020. Interest payments are due on April&#160;1, and
    October&#160;1, commencing April&#160;1, 2006. The debentures
    will be convertible, under certain circumstances at the
    holders&#146; option, into shares of the Company&#146;s
    Class&#160;A common stock initially at a conversion rate of
    97.0685&#160;shares per $1,000 principal amount of the
    debentures (equivalent to an initial conversion price of
    approximately $10.30 per share), subject to adjustments related
    to potential equity transactions and other events. Upon
    conversion of the debentures, the Company has the right to
    deliver shares of its Class&#160;A common stock, cash or a
    combination of cash and shares of its Class&#160;A common stock.
    The debentures are effectively subordinated to DCC&#146;s
    existing and future secured indebtedness to the extent of the
    collateral securing that indebtedness, and to the existing and
    future liabilities of DCC&#146;s subsidiaries; equal in right of
    payment to all of DCC&#146;s existing and future unsecured
    senior indebtedness; and senior in right of payment to
    DCC&#146;s future subordinated indebtedness.

    operating assets.&#148;
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 9pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Commitments</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On August&#160;29, 2006, the Company amended its purchase and
    license agreement with Nortel Networks Corp. Under the purchase
    and license agreement with Nortel Networks Corp., the Company
    has a commitment to make specified minimum purchases of GSM
    related products and services prior to December&#160;31, 2008.
    If the Company fails to achieve this commitment, the agreement
    provides for liquidated damages in an amount equal to 5% of the
    portion of the unfulfilled commitment. As of December&#160;31,
    2006, the exposure for such damages is approximately
    $1.1&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 9pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Contingencies</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company has reached an agreement to settle the previously
    disclosed consolidated securities class action pending in the
    United States District Court for the Western District of
    Oklahoma. The settlement agreement, which is subject to court
    approval, would resolve all pending claims against the Company
    and all named individual defendants and includes all persons who
    purchased the Company&#146;s publicly traded securities between
    May&#160;6, 2003 and August&#160;9, 2004. Lead counsel for the
    class has filed a motion seeking court approval of the
    settlement. The Court on December&#160;11, 2006 granted
    preliminary approval of the settlement. The final approval
    hearing is set for March&#160;20, 2007. On December&#160;26,
    2006, notice of the terms of the settlement was sent to all
    known potential class members. Any objections to the class
    settlement must be filed by February&#160;14, 2007. The
    settlement provides for $3.4&#160;million to be paid to settle
    claims submitted by class members and the plaintiffs&#146;
    attorneys&#146; fees. A substantial portion of the settlement
    amount is covered by insurance.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company is party to various other legal actions arising in
    the normal course of business. None of these actions are
    believed by management to involve amounts that will be material
    to its consolidated financial position, results of operation or
    liquidity.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company is not currently aware of any additional or material
    changes to pending or threatened litigation against it or its
    subsidiaries or that involves any of it or its subsidiaries
    property that could have a material adverse effect on its
    financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Issuance
    of Preferred Stock</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company issued 175,000&#160;shares of 12.25% preferred stock
    in April 1998 and 64,646&#160;shares of additional 12.25%
    preferred stock in December 1998, mandatorily redeemable on
    January&#160;15, 2008 for $1,000&#160;per share plus accrued
    dividends. At December&#160;31, 2006, all of the Company&#146;s
    12.25% preferred stock had been redeemed.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In May 1999, the Company issued 170,000&#160;shares of 13%
    preferred stock mandatorily redeemable on May&#160;1, 2009 for
    $1,000&#160;per share. At December&#160;31, 2006, all of the
    Company&#146;s 13% preferred stock had been redeemed.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company issued 686,201&#160;shares of Series&#160;F
    preferred stock on August&#160;18, 2003, mandatorily redeemable
    on August&#160;18, 2016, for $178.571&#160;per share. Holders of
    the preferred stock are entitled to cumulative dividends from
    the date of issuance and a liquidation preference of
    $178.571&#160;per share. In addition, the preferred stock is
    convertible at the option of the holder, making it a
    conditionally redeemable instrument until August&#160;18, 2016.
    The Company may pay dividends at its option, at 6% in cash or at
    7% in additional shares of Series&#160;F preferred stock. The
    preferred stock was redeemable at the option of the Company in
    whole or in part on and after August&#160;18, 2005. Holders of
    the preferred stock have no voting rights. Each share of the
    Company&#146;s Series&#160;F preferred stock is convertible into
    the Company&#146;s Class&#160;A common stock at a conversion
    rate of $8.75&#160;per Class&#160;A common share, subject to
    adjustment from time to time. On September&#160;12, 2005, the
    Company issued 48,015&#160;shares of Series&#160;F preferred
    stock as payment in kind for dividends due on October&#160;15,
    2004 and April&#160;15, 2005 on its outstanding Series&#160;F
    preferred stock. The Company also paid accrued interest on those
    dividends. On October&#160;15, 2005, the Company issued
    25,680&#160;shares of Series&#160;F preferred stock as payment
    in kind for dividends due October&#160;15, 2005 on its
    outstanding Series&#160;F preferred stock. The Company has made
    cash dividend payments since that time. At December&#160;31,
    2006, the Company had a total liquidation preference value of
    $135.7&#160;million, plus accrued dividends on its Series&#160;F
    preferred stock.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 9pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Repurchases
    of Preferred Stock</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On June&#160;15, 2004, the Company&#146;s board of directors
    authorized it to expend up to $50.0&#160;million to repurchase
    some of the Company&#146;s outstanding 12.25% and
    13%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred stock. Through
    June&#160;30, 2005 (prior to the completion of the
    Company&#146;s exchange offer described below), the Company
    repurchased a total of 14,816&#160;shares of 12.25%&#160;senior
    exchangeable preferred stock and 9,475&#160;shares of
    13%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred stock. The preferred
    stock repurchases totaled 24,291&#160;shares for
    $17.4&#160;million, all of which have been canceled. These
    repurchases resulted in a gain on redemption and repurchases of
    preferred stock totaling $6.5&#160;million for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2004.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 9pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Exchange
    Offer</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On August&#160;23, 2005, the Company completed an exchange offer
    with holders of its 12.25%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred
    stock and its 13%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred stock. In
    connection with the exchange offer, the Company issued
    28,249,729&#160;shares of Class&#160;A common stock and paid
    $50.2&#160;million in cash for an aggregate of
    167,356&#160;shares of preferred stock. All 167,356&#160;shares
    of the preferred stock repurchased have been canceled. The
    Company incurred a loss on this transaction of approximately
    $66.4&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;4, 2005, the Company entered into agreements
    with certain holders of its 12.25%&#160;senior exchangeable
    preferred stock and its 13%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred
    stock under which the holders agreed to
    exchange&#160;8,700&#160;shares of 12.25%&#160;senior
    exchangeable preferred stock and 30,021&#160;shares of 13%
    senior exchangeable preferred stock for 5,982,040&#160;shares of
    the Company&#146;s Class&#160;A common stock and cash
    consideration of $1.6&#160;million. Upon the closing of these
    transactions, the aggregate outstanding liquidation preference
    of the 12.25%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred stock and the
    13%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred stock decreased from
    $71.7&#160;million to $33.0&#160;million. The Company reported a
    loss on this transaction of approximately $4.4&#160;million in
    the fourth quarter of 2005.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Redemption
    of Preferred Stock</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On March&#160;1, 2006, for cash consideration of
    $41.7&#160;million, the Company redeemed and cancelled all
    remaining outstanding shares of its 12.25%&#160;senior
    exchangeable preferred stock and its 13%&#160;senior
    exchangeable preferred stock.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The cash redemption price for the 12.25%&#160;senior
    exchangeable preferred stock was $1,220.38&#160;per share, which
    represents 100% of the liquidation preference, plus an amount in
    cash equal to all accrued dividends (including applicable
    interest for accrued dividends) up to, but not including, the
    redemption date. The cash redemption price for the
    13%&#160;senior exchangeable preferred stock was
    $1,270.98&#160;per share, which represents 104.333% of the
    liquidation preference, plus an amount in cash equal to all
    accrued dividends (including applicable interest for accrued
    dividends) up to, but not including, the redemption date. The
    Company recorded a loss of approximately $1.5&#160;million
    during 2006 as a result of these redemptions.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 9pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Dividends
    on Preferred Stock</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company recorded dividends on its mandatorily redeemable
    preferred stock of $32.1&#160;million for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2004, which are included in the Company&#146;s
    net loss. These dividends consist of $5.2&#160;million of cash
    dividends paid on its 12.25% preferred stock, $0.6&#160;million
    of accrued dividends on its 12.25% preferred stock,
    $19.5&#160;million of cash dividends paid on its 13% preferred
    stock and $6.8&#160;million of accrued dividends on its 13%
    preferred stock. The Company recorded dividends on its
    conditionally redeemable preferred stock of $8.2&#160;million
    for the year ended December&#160;31, 2004, which consisted of
    $3.7&#160;million of cash dividends and $4.5&#160;million of
    accrued dividends on its Series&#160;F preferred stock and are
    included in determining the Company&#146;s net loss applicable
    to common stockholders.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company recorded dividends on its mandatorily redeemable
    preferred stock of $22.6&#160;million for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2005, which are included in the Company&#146;s
    net loss. These dividends consist of $4.4&#160;million of
    accrued dividends on its 12.25% preferred stock and
    $18.2&#160;million of accrued dividends on its 13% preferred
    stock. The Company recorded dividends on its conditionally
    redeemable preferred stock of $9.1&#160;million for the year
    ended December&#160;31, 2005, which consisted of accrued
    dividends on its Series&#160;F preferred stock. The
    Company&#146;s dividends on its conditionally redeemable
    preferred stock are included in determining the Company&#146;s
    net loss applicable to common stockholders.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company recorded dividends on its mandatorily redeemable
    preferred stock of $0.7&#160;million for the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2006, which are included in determining the
    Company&#146;s net income. The Company recorded dividends on its
    conditionally redeemable preferred stock of $8.5&#160;million
    for the year ended December&#160;31, 2006, which consisted of
    $8.1&#160;million of cash dividends and $0.4&#160;million of
    accrued dividends on its Series&#160;F preferred stock. The
    Company&#146;s dividends on its conditionally redeemable
    preferred stock are included in determining the Company&#146;s
    net loss applicable to common stockholders.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Each share of the Company&#146;s Class&#160;B common stock is
    convertible into one share of Class&#160;A common stock and each
    share of the Company&#146;s Class&#160;C common stock and
    Class&#160;D common stock is convertible into 111.44&#160;shares
    of Class&#160;A common stock at the option of the holder. Due to
    these conversion features, the Company&#146;s calculation of its
    weighted average common shares outstanding is performed on an as
    converted basis. In addition, each share of the Company&#146;s
    Class&#160;B common stock is entitled to 10 votes and each share
    of Class&#160;A common stock is entitled to one vote.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Additional shares of the Company&#146;s Class&#160;A common
    stock have been reserved for issuance under the Company&#146;s
    benefit plans. See Note&#160;10 for discussion of the
    Company&#146;s employee stock incentive plans and employee stock
    purchase plan.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">401(k)
    Plan</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company maintains a 401(k) plan, or the Plan, in which
    substantially all employees whom have greater than one year of
    service are eligible to participate. The Plan requires the
    Company to match 100% of employees&#146; contributions up to 4%
    of their salary. Contributions to the Plan charged to operations
    were $1.9&#160;million during the year ended December&#160;31,
    2006, $1.9&#160;million during the year ended December&#160;31,
    2005 and $1.7&#160;million during the year ended
    December&#160;31, 2004 and were recorded as general and
    administrative expenses.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 9pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Stock
    Option Plans</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company adopted its 1996 stock option plan, or the 1996
    plan, its 2000 stock option plan, or the 2000 plan, and its 2002
    stock option plan, or the 2002 plan, to encourage its key
    employees by providing opportunities to participate in the
    ownership and future growth of the Company through the grant of
    incentive stock options and nonqualified stock options. The
    plans also permit the grant of options to the Company&#146;s
    directors. The Company&#146;s compensation committee presently
    administers the 1996, 2000 and 2002 plans. Through
    December&#160;31, 2005, the Company accounted for the plans
    under APB Opinion&#160;25, under which no compensation cost was
    recognized in the accompanying consolidated financial statements
    if the option price was equal to or greater than the fair market
    value of the stock at the time the option was granted. Beginning
    January&#160;1, 2006, the Company began accounting for the plans
    under SFAS&#160;123(R), under which compensation cost is
    recognized, as discussed in Note&#160;3.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under the 1996 plan, the board of directors granted both
    incentive and non-incentive stock options for employees,
    officers and directors to acquire Class&#160;C common stock and
    Class&#160;D common stock, which is convertible into shares of
    Class&#160;A common stock at a 111.44 to 1 basis at the time of
    exercise. Options granted under the 2000 and 2002 plans can also
    be both incentive and non-incentive stock options for employees,
    officers and directors; however, all options granted under these
    plans are to purchase shares of Class&#160;A common stock.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under all the plans, stock options have been issued at the
    market price on the date of grant with an expiration of ten
    years from the grant date. All options vest at either a rate of
    20% or 25%&#160;per year. The maximum number of

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Stock
    Purchase Plan</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Dobson Communications Corporation 2002 Employee Stock
    Purchase Plan, or the Purchase Plan, was approved at the 2002
    Annual Meeting of Stockholders. The Purchase Plan provides for
    1,000,000&#160;shares of the Company&#146;s Class&#160;A common
    stock to be reserved for issuance upon exercise of purchase
    rights which may be granted under the Purchase Plan, subject to
    adjustment for stock dividends, stock splits, reverse stock
    splits and similar changes in the Company&#146;s capitalization.
    The Purchase Plan is designed to encourage stock ownership by
    employees. Employees elect to participate in the plan
    semi-annually. The plan period is six months. Shares are
    purchased at 85% of the market price of the Company&#146;s
    Class&#160;A common stock. The price is determined as the
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    79
</DIV><!-- END LOGICAL PAGE -->

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    At December&#160;31, 2006, the Company had federal loss
    carryforwards of approximately $968&#160;million, which may be
    utilized to reduce future federal income taxes payable. These
    loss carryforwards expire from 2019 to 2026, including
    $468&#160;million expiring in 2023.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The Company periodically reviews the need for a valuation
    allowance against deferred tax assets. This includes a review of
    historical taxable results, financial operating income and
    leverage trends, tax attributes, forecasted taxable income prior
    to the expiration of the loss carryforwards and the long-term
    character of the expiration dates of those carryforwards. The
    Company has had taxable losses in the past as a result of
    accelerated depreciation on its property, plant and equipment,
    from the tax amortization on its wireless licenses, an
    indefinite life intangible asset for financial purposes, and
    from financing costs. These taxable losses resulted in the
    Company&#146;s loss carryforwards. The Company has provided a
    valuation allowance for certain of its deferred tax assets.
    After consideration of the valuation allowance, the Company
    believes that it is more likely than not of realizing its
    deferred tax asset, including the projection of sufficient
    taxable income to recover its net deferred tax asset exclusive
    of its wireless licenses which are not amortized for financial
    accounting. Based on this review and the annual changes in the
    above factors, the valuation allowance was decreased by
    $13.8&#160;million during 2006. In addition, as a result of
    changes in certain state corporate tax statutes and other items,
    the Company reduced its total deferred tax liability by
    approximately $2.0&#160;million. Both the change in valuation
    allowance and the reduction in deferred tax liabilities due to
    changes in state tax statutes were reflected in the
    Company&#146;s income from continuing operations.
</DIV>

    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">14.&#160;&#160;</FONT></B>
</TD>
    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">STAFF
    ACCOUNTING BULLETIN&#160;NO.&#160;108:</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As discussed in Note&#160;2, the SEC released
    SAB&#160;No.&#160;108 in September 2006. SAB&#160;No.&#160;108
    requires all companies to consider errors using both a
    current-year and a cumulative approach. Previously, the Company
    considered its errors using a current year effect basis.
    SAB&#160;No.&#160;108 permits the Company to adjust for the
    cumulative effect of immaterial errors relating to prior years
    in the carrying amount of assets and liabilities as of the
    beginning of the current fiscal year, with an offsetting
    adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings in the
    year of adoption. The Company adopted SAB&#160;No.&#160;108 and
    adjusted its opening retained earnings for 2006 to reflect a
    change in its accounting for leases. Prior to 2006, the Company
    did not record the effects of scheduled rent increases on a
    straight-line basis for certain real estate leases. Therefore,
    the Company adjusted its opening retained earnings for the year
    ended 2006 by approximately $5.0&#160;million, net of income
    tax, to reflect a change in its accounting for leases. The
    Company reviewed the annual amount of additional expense
    incurred in prior periods and considers this adjustment to be
    immaterial to prior periods.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    CONDENSED CONSOLIDATING FINANCIAL INFORMATION:</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Set forth below is supplemental condensed consolidating
    financial information as required by DCC&#146;s indenture for
    its 8.875%&#160;senior notes due 2013, and by the DCS credit
    facility. The statement of operations information is presented
    without parent recognition of subsidiary results. Included are
    the condensed consolidating balance sheets of the Company as of
    December&#160;31, 2006 and 2005 and the statements of operations
    and statements of cash flows of the Company for the years ended
    December&#160;31, 2006, 2005 and 2004. Neither DCS, ACC, the
    non-guarantor subsidiaries, nor any of their subsidiaries
    guarantee any of DCC&#146;s debt securities. DCC, DCS and its
    subsidiaries do not guarantee any of ACC&#146;s outstanding
    debt. Neither DCC, the non-guarantor subsidiaries, nor ACC and
    its subsidiaries guarantee any of DCS&#146; outstanding debt
    securities. However, DCS&#146; subsidiaries do guarantee
    DCS&#146; debt securities. See Note&#160;6 for a description of
    the Company&#146;s debt securities.

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">SUBSEQUENT
    EVENT:</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On February&#160;15, 2007, ACC commenced a cash tender offer for
    any and all of its $900.0&#160;million aggregate principal
    amount of 10.0%&#160;senior notes due 2011, and a consent
    solicitation to amend the terms of these senior notes and
    related indenture. The purpose of the consent solicitation is to
    amend the terms of ACC&#146;s 10.0%&#160;senior notes and the
    related indenture, to remove substantially all of the
    restrictive covenants contained therein.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    This tender offer is part of a proposed refinancing of
    ACC&#146;s existing 10.0%&#160;senior notes, its
    $18.1&#160;million aggregate principal amount of
    9.5%&#160;senior subordinated notes due 2009 and
    $124.7&#160;million outstanding under its existing senior
    secured credit facility, or the refinancing. ACC expects to
    finance the refinancing through new indebtedness consisting of
    notes and a term loan credit facility.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The tender offer and refinancing are subject to the satisfaction
    of certain conditions and there can be no assurance it will be
    completed on satisfactory terms or at all.
</DIV>

    reviewed the annual amount of additional expense incurred in

    this adjustment to be immaterial to prior periods.

    stock and the fourth quarter of 2005 includes a
    $4.4&#160;million loss on redemption and repurchases of
    mandatorily redeemable preferred stock. The per share effect of

    quarter of 2005 and $0.03 for the fourth quarter of 2005.

    quarter of 2005.

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Conclusion
    Regarding the Effectiveness of Disclosure Controls and
    Procedures</FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under the supervision and with the participation of our
    management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief
    Financial Officer, we evaluated the design and operation of our
    disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">Rules&#160;13a-15(e)</FONT>
    and
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">15d-15(e)</FONT> of
    the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, or the &#147;Exchange
    Act&#148;) as of December&#160;31, 2006. On the basis of this
    review, our management, including our Chief Executive Officer
    and Chief Financial Officer, concluded that our disclosure
    controls and procedures are designed, and are effective, to give
    reasonable assurance that the information required to be
    disclosed by us in reports that we file under the Exchange Act
    is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time
    periods specified in the rules and forms of the SEC and to
    ensure that information required to be disclosed in the reports
    filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and
    communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive
    Officer and Chief Financial Officer, in a manner that allows
    timely decisions regarding required disclosure.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    There were no changes in our internal control over financial
    reporting during the fourth quarter of 2006 that materially
    affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our
    internal control over financial reporting.
</DIV>
